narratives.name: Platform Foundation Context
narratives.description: Why the platform foundation matters for developer productivity.

narrativeContexts.context: The platform foundation represents the technical substrate upon which all developer-facing capabilities are built, progressing from architecture selection through operational maturity to eventual retirement.

Platform architecture encompasses compute, networking, storage, identity, security, and observability foundations that collectively enable the thirteen CNCF capability domains through infrastructure-as-code and automated provisioning.

CNCF research demonstrates that organizations with mature platform foundations achieve elite DORA metrics, with provisioning times measured in minutes rather than days and deployment frequencies measured in multiple daily deployments per team.

Platform foundation maturity is measured through operational reliability, self-service capability breadth, cost optimization effectiveness, and the ability to evolve proactively based on predictive analytics and continuous user feedback.

narratives.name: Practice Intent
narratives.description: Narrative describing the platform engineering transformation journey.

narrativeContexts.context: Organizations operate with fragmented infrastructure, duplicated tooling across teams, and developers burdened by undifferentiated infrastructure work consuming approximately 45% of cognitive capacity.
Leadership recognizes the organizational cost of fragmented approaches and the CNCF platform engineering guidance provides a proven path toward reduced cognitive load and accelerated delivery.
Platform teams face adoption challenges navigating the DORA J-Curve while building self-service capabilities, establishing product management discipline, and demonstrating value through metrics.

Organizations master platform engineering demonstrating reduced cognitive load, accelerated delivery, elite DORA metrics, and platform teams serving as organizational multipliers through participatory ecosystems.

narratives.name: Capability Domain Context
narratives.description: Why platform capabilities matter for developer productivity.

narrativeContexts.context: Platform capabilities represent distinct service domains that collectively enable developer productivity and organizational agility through self-service infrastructure provisioning.

The CNCF defines thirteen capability domains spanning compute, networking, security, identity, artifacts, observability, data, messaging, and more, each requiring evaluation of build versus buy decisions and abstraction levels.
Capabilities mature from identified needs through designed interfaces and implemented automation to governed operations and optimized performance based on usage patterns and user feedback loops.
Optimized capabilities serve as reference patterns demonstrating best practices that inform implementation of additional capability domains, accelerating platform maturity across the organization.

narratives.name: Product Management Evolution
narratives.description: How product management discipline transforms platform value delivery.

narrativeContexts.context: Platform product management transforms infrastructure from cost center to value driver by treating internal users as customers deserving systematic product management attention and investment.

Product management discipline for platforms encompasses user research through developer experience surveys, roadmap development using impact-weighted prioritization, and value measurement through DORA metrics and satisfaction tracking.

Dedicated product managers apply user research, roadmap development, and value measurement creating clear value propositions that attract self-sustaining adoption through participatory ecosystems where users become contributors.

Ecosystem-enabled platforms achieve maximum organizational leverage as core teams provide foundations enabling specialists to extend capabilities, demonstrating success through user satisfaction and measurable business outcomes.
